GPU processing¶

wvt can calculate these items on the GPU:

  • The file waterfall.

  • The live spectrum.

  • The channel filter of the time plots and of the region export.

wvt supports CUDA on an NVIDIA GPU under Linux, and Metal on an Apple GPU under macOS. With a GPU, wide views can keep “FFT sees 100 %”, and the live spectrum can analyze all samples at USRP rates. The results are the same as on the CPU.

NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA, Linux)¶

Build:

  • The CUDA toolkit 12.0 or later. For RTX 50-series GPUs, use 12.8 or later.

  • CMake 3.18 or later.

  • CMake finds nvcc and shows wvt: CUDA support enabled (CUDA 12.x, archs ..., static cuFFT).

Run:

  • An NVIDIA driver.

  • A GPU with compute capability 7.5 or later (GeForce RTX 20xx and newer).

  • A minimum of 1 GB of free GPU memory.

A CUDA build also runs on computers without a GPU or a driver. wvt then uses the CPU, and the log tells you why.

Apple GPUs (Metal, macOS)¶

Build: you do not have to install more software. The Command Line Tools are sufficient. You do not need Xcode. CMake shows wvt: Metal support enabled.

Run:

  • macOS 14 or later. Older versions use the CPU.

  • The kernels compile when wvt uses the GPU for the first time (approximately 0.2 s).

On a Mac, the CPU path uses the Accelerate FFT (vDSP). Thus the CPU is also fast. On an M5, the GPU gives these speeds, compared with the CPU:

Job

Speed

Waterfall, N ≤ 4096

Approximately 1.6 times

One live row

2.5 to 3.4 times

Channel filter with many taps

Up to 6 times

Small jobs stay on the CPU.

For the CMake options, refer to Build reference.

Select the GPU at run time¶

Control

Function

--gpu auto

Use a GPU if one is usable. This is the default

--gpu on

Use the GPU. If no GPU is usable, wvt stops

--gpu off

Do not use the GPU. wvt does not load the driver

WVT_GPU

The environment variable for the same values

--gpu-device N

Use GPU N

--list-devices

Show the GPUs and the SDR devices

Tools → Use the GPU

Disable or enable the GPU in the window

The status bar shows GPU <model> or CPU. The tooltip of each view tells you where wvt calculated it.

Errors¶

If a GPU error occurs, that part of wvt goes back to the CPU for the rest of the session. The log and the status-bar tooltip tell you why.

To test the fallback without an error, set WVT_GPU_FORCE_FAIL=1. Each GPU call then fails, and wvt uses the CPU.

Check the GPU¶

  • build/gpu_check compares the GPU results with the CPU results.

  • build/gpu_check --bench measures the speed of the GPU and the CPU.

How it works¶

src/gpu/gpu.h is the interface that the rest of wvt uses. src/gpu/gpu_common.cpp applies the --gpu rules and the fallback to the CPU. Each backend implements the interface in src/gpu/gpu_backend.h:

Backend

File

FFT

CUDA

src/gpu/gpu_cuda.cu

cuFFT

Metal

src/gpu/gpu_metal.mm

FFTs up to 4096 points in one pass in the on-chip memory of the GPU. Larger FFTs use MPSGraph

None

src/gpu/gpu_stub.cpp

The CPU only

On a Mac, the GPU reads the memory-mapped file in place, because the CPU and the GPU share the memory. wvt sends a job to the GPU only when the job is sufficiently large. Each job type has its own work limit.

For the designs, refer to the CUDA design record and the Apple GPU design record.
